content:
As AI agents rapidly emerge, coupled with a surge in requests for full Mac disk access, Apple says it will adjust macOS to protect user privacy.

Although Apple has not yet revealed specific details, it emphasises that users should understand the true implications of granting such 'extremely high' permissions to applications.

In a blog post on its developer website, Apple explained that full disk access in macOS was originally designed to 'let backup apps work properly on a Mac.' However, Apple noted that 'some developers' are using macOS's full disk access settings in ways that 'could put users at risk.'

Apple said it will 'introduce additional safeguards to ensure that users who genuinely intend to grant extremely high levels of access to an app must do so through a very explicit confirmation action.'

The company did not provide further details on these safeguards or the specific changes. However, Apple pointed out that the rise of 'increasingly powerful and autonomous' AI agents makes privacy and security a greater concern:

Apple's announcement comes as tools like Meta Muse and OpenAI's Dots grow increasingly popular. These always-on AI agents demand access to vast amounts of personal data, and we have already seen some troubling cases involving Meta Muse.
